explanations: The yolk is the nutrient-bearing part, stored food rich in vitamins, minerals, lipids and proteins, there to feed the growing embryo.
The white, or albumen, is about 90 per cent water with 10 per cent protein and almost no fat, and whisks up into meringue and mousse.
The shell is the protective covering, flexible or rigid, around the eggs of reptiles, birds and monotremes.
Yolk, white and shell are the three parts of an egg, the vessel an animal grows to carry a fertilised egg cell.

sources.excerpt: Among animals which produce eggs, the yolk (; also known as the vitellus) is the nutrient-bearing portion of the egg, the primary function of which is to supply food for the development of the embryo.
As stored food, yolks are often rich in vitamins, minerals, lipids and proteins.
Egg white consists of about 90% water into which about 10% proteins (including albumins, mucoproteins, and globulins) are dissolved.
Egg white has many uses in food (e.g. meringue, mousse) as well as many other uses (e.g. in the preparation of vaccines such as those for influenza).
Reptile eggs, bird eggs, and monotreme eggs are laid out of water and are surrounded by a protective shell, either flexible or inflexible.
Some embryos have a temporary egg tooth they use to crack, pip, or break the eggshell or covering.
An egg is an organic vessel grown by an animal to carry a possibly fertilized egg cell – a zygote.
